meta.title: 06.11.2026 Cea mai dura sesiune din ultimile 19 luni.
meta.thread_line: 7 threads · worst session in 19 months · AI-ban talk, data centers and the cost of AI · 2018 vs April 2025 playbook · his one move: Vertiv on margin · SpaceX and Oracle below key levels · AMD, Broadcom, Nebius and IREN · NFP day scenarios and the rest of the book

snapshot: Source note: built from GrowYourWealth's pasted written note of Nov 6 (no video), the morning after the crash, so figures are as the author states them.
Nov 5 was the worst Nasdaq session in about 19 months (**-5.52%**, now in correction) and the worst S&P 500 day since the April 2025 tariff shock (-4.36%); over $4T erased, VIX +70%, SOX down 12%+.
He discloses his portfolio lost **$372,000** in one session, its largest drop ever, and says he sold nothing.

His read: a sudden sentiment shift on top of excessive leverage, triggered by Democratic lawmakers calling for AI restrictions up to a superintelligence ban; he says a total ban will not happen and calls the drop technical, not fundamental.
His one move: 200 VRT at $178 (~$35,000), bought on margin after refusing it above $200; ORCL was re-added in recent days and CRWD and NET are on his re-entry list.
Base case: closer to April 2025 (a fast V-shaped recovery) than late 2018, with a possible year-end rally, his opinion, not a certainty.
Damage: AMD -17.26% despite a strong quarter, AVGO -10.43%, TSLA -10.77%, SPCX -9.05%, ORCL -6.93% and below its $116 issue price; FT reports Oracle walked away from a ~$7B Tencent deal.
NFP day plan: consensus ~59,000 jobs and 4.2% unemployment; he held back cash, and S&P 500 7,350 and Nasdaq 24,300 are his warning levels.

themes.status: NASDAQ -5.52% · S&P 500 -4.36% · >$4T ERASED · 85% OF S&P DOWN
themes.title: Worst session in 19 months: market-wide de-risking, not a few overvalued names
themes.lead: Nov 5 hit almost everything at once, and the author's own portfolio lost $372,000 in a day, the largest drop it has ever recorded.
bullets: Nasdaq entered correction, more than 10% below its Oct 6 high, with its worst daily drop in about 19 months; the S&P's worst session since the April 2025 tariff shock.
Over $4T wiped off the market, a figure not seen since the 2020 Covid crash; VIX's 70% one-day jump was the fifth largest in stock-market history.

Breadth: of ~499 S&P 500 components tracked by one data source, 426 fell and 73 rose (~85% down); tech -7.7%, communication services held up relatively better, Philadelphia Semiconductor index down over 12%.

Inside damage: nearly 50% of US stocks trade at least 30% below 52-week highs, ~70% (almost 4,000 companies) are in a bear market versus record highs, 2,600 are down 70%+ and 2,200 of those more than **80%**.

Funds hit hard in one day: Situational Awareness, Walleye, Axebrook, Engineers Gate, Lone Pine, Samlyn and various Verition units; he says Warren Buffett, Stanley Druckenmiller and David Tepper also lost heavily.
His own book: -$372,000 in one session, disclosed publicly; he says the pain across the community weighs on him too.

themes.status: AI-BAN TALK · DATA-CENTER LIMITS · 10Y 4.836% · OIL UP
themes.title: What changed: AI-ban talk, data-center limits and a market repricing the cost of AI
themes.lead: The midterm result was largely priced in, so he points to AI-regulation fear landing on an over-levered market and calls the drop technical rather than fundamental.
bullets: Likely trigger: in the prior 24 hours Democratic lawmakers publicly called for restrictions on advanced AI development, including a **total ban on superintelligence**.
His view: a total ban will not happen, since it would hand China the global AI race and nobody in Washington will do that, whatever the party; regulation worries are still legitimate.
Mechanism: a sudden sentiment shift layered on excessive leverage can force big institutional liquidations, so price action is neither orderly nor rational right now.

Data centers: a Democratic Congress shifts expectations for limits on building, energy use and resources, the area behind much of 2026's market gains; Reuters says data-center fears were one of the main drivers, but possible limits do not mean existing projects are halted.

Cost of AI: investors now separate firms already making cash from AI from those spending billions before revenue, which is why AMD, Broadcom and Nvidia fell together despite very different business models.
Rates: yields fell on safe-haven demand (10Y ~4.836%, 2Y 4.475%, ~36bp spread), but risk aversion dominated; lower rates do not lift stocks when earnings estimates and confidence deteriorate.

Fed officials raised the chance of staying restrictive and even future hikes if inflation requires, with no new Fed decision Thursday; oil rose, partly reversing recent drops, which complicates the inflation outlook.

themes.status: 2018: -19.8%, RECOVERED IN 4 MONTHS · APR 2025: +9.5% IN A DAY
themes.title: April 2025, not late 2018: his base case, and a five-step checklist for the days after
themes.lead: He leans on two past drawdowns and Buffett to argue for patience, and gives followers a concrete checklist instead of reassurance.
bullets: 2018: from the September high to the Dec 24 low the S&P 500 lost ~19.8% (US-China trade war, global slowdown fears, a restrictive Fed); it fully recovered by Apr 23, 2019, four months from extreme pessimism to highs.

April 2025: after Trump's tariffs the S&P fell ~18.9% from its February high to an Apr 8 low; on Apr 9 a 90-day pause sent it up ~9.5% in one session and the Nasdaq 12%+, and by early June it was 20%+ off the low. Yesterday reminds him of that day.

Worst case: a 2018 repeat (S&P -16% from Oct 1 to Dec 15, individual portfolios -50-60%, slow recovery over four to five months); his view is we are closer to April 2025, with a possible **year-end rally**, opinion not certainty.

Buffett: nobody can catch the bottom; when you buy a stock be ready for it to fall 50% or more. Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.B) fell 50% three times with nothing wrong with the business; those who suffer bought on debt or react to every price move.

Checklist: (1) test the thesis, not the price: results, competitive edge, growth outlook, balance sheet, and whether your exposure fits your risk; (2) check cumulative exposure, not single weights; (3) buy selectively and in stages, conditioned on price stabilization; (4) keep a liquidity reserve suited to you; (5) no permanent decisions on temporary emotions.
Cumulative exposure: AMD, Broadcom, Oracle, Nebius and IREN can all be hit by an AI-spending repricing; SPCX, RKLB and ASTS move together on space-sector risk perception.
Don'ts: panic-selling at support, buying with all your cash before NFP, or changing a ten-year strategy after ten hours of volatility.

themes.title: One move, not ten: Vertiv re-enters the portfolio at a price he refused days earlier
themes.lead: He bought the power-and-cooling supplier behind AI chips after a 25% two-day drop, sold nothing else, and kept the rest of his cash for NFP day.
bullets: Trade: **200 VRT at $178** (~$35,000), using margin, after refusing to pay over $200; he bought only after it broke the $192 support, not at $235, and not his full intended size. ORCL was re-added in recent days; CRWD and NET are on his re-entry list at set prices.

Nothing sold: no cut to AMD, SPCX, TSLA, PLTR or META, and he did not touch Nebius or IREN; no aggressive buying elsewhere ahead of NFP in a book already concentrated in AI infrastructure, semis and space.

Business: power, cooling and continuous-operation gear for data centers, the infrastructure chips need to run; co-developed with NVIDIA the full power and cooling solution for GB200 NVL72; it gains whether Nvidia, AMD or hyperscaler custom accelerators lead.
Q3 2026 (reported Oct 28): revenue $4.31B (+61% y/y), organic orders over +100%, adjusted operating margin 25.2% (+2.9 pts), adjusted EPS $2.21 (+78%), adjusted free cash flow $652M (+50%).

Management's 2026 guidance: revenue $14.45-14.85B, adjusted EPS $7.10-7.20, adjusted FCF $2.6-2.8B; it aims to double chiller production capacity by end-2026 as denser racks push air cooling past its limits toward liquid cooling, UPS and modular builds.

Valuation: Nov 5 close $176.69 (-14.04%), down ~25% from $235.97 on Nov 3; market cap ~$68B, trailing P/E ~33, ~24.7x guided 2026 adjusted EPS (not a GAAP P/E). His November 2028 scenarios: bear $153 (-13%), base $263 (+49%), bull $375 (+112%).

Risks: slower hyperscaler spending, project delays, production problems, competition, energy or regulatory limits. Technicals: $170.80 Nov 5 low, first resistance $195-205; he treats VRT as staged accumulation conditional on price stabilizing and orders confirming.

themes.title: SpaceX and Oracle: political risk and financing risk, both trading below their markers
themes.lead: His strategic priority SpaceX fell on Musk-oversight fears he separates from operations, while Oracle broke its issue price and picked up a new China-deal headline.
bullets: SPCX closed **$123.62** (-9.05%), range $120.39-131.87, volume over 172 million shares; investors are repricing closer political oversight of Musk-linked companies, which does not show lost contracts or weaker Starlink.

Starlink is one of the most important assets for the GYW portfolio thanks to recurring connectivity revenue and integration with launches, but valuation must reflect constellation capex, competition and cash conversion.

SPCX levels: support $120-121, resistance $131-132 then $135-136; back above $132 is a first stabilization signal, losing $120.39 means selling pressure persists. No confirmation the correction is over.

ORCL closed $115.16 (-6.93%), range $111.66-124.24, volume over 57 million, below the $116 issue price of its ~$20B equity-plus-bond raise; an issue price is not guaranteed support. The equity adds dilution, the debt adds interest.
His four Oracle metrics: OCI growth, capex, free cash flow and cost of financing.

Financial Times: Oracle dropped an estimated **$7B** deal with Tencent for up to 100,000 AI accelerators in Southeast Asian data centers over five years, with US pressure contributing; Reuters could not independently verify it. An estimated contract value is not $7B of recognized revenue or loss.
ORCL levels: immediate support $111-112, first recovery marker $116, secondary resistance $121-124.

themes.status: AMD $404.40 (-17.26%) · AVGO -10.43% · IREN FQ1 AI CLOUD +182% Q/Q
themes.title: AMD and Broadcom get de-rated despite strong demand, while Nebius and IREN live on financing
themes.lead: Strong results did not protect the chipmakers from multiple compression, and for the AI-cloud builders financing is now the main variable.
bullets: AMD closed ~**$404.40** (-17.26%) the same week it reported Q3 revenue ~$13.4B (+45% y/y) and data center ~$8.5B (+97%); if investors expect slower hyperscaler spending, multiples fall even as revenue grows. He sees no verified evidence the results broke the thesis.
Broadcom fell ~10.43% and weighed heavily on the S&P 500: big exposure to custom AI accelerators and networking, with software diversifying revenue.

Nebius (NBIS) is among the most sentiment-sensitive AI-infrastructure names (heavy GPU, data-center and energy spend), and short seller Citron Research told its clients to short NBIS; he weighs contract value against utilization, margins and funding needs.

IREN (Reuters lists it among infrastructure operators down over 14%) reported FQ1 FY2027 (to Sep 30) vs the prior quarter: revenue $228M vs $137M (+66%), AI Cloud $200M vs $71M (+182%), Bitcoin mining $28M vs $67M (-58%), adjusted EBITDA $66M vs $19M (margin 29% vs 14%), GAAP net loss $263M vs $684M, AI Cloud gross margin 86%, revenue backlog $20.3B vs ~$16.6B (+22%).

AI Cloud is now ~88% of revenue (from ~52%); year on year total revenue still slipped from ~$240M to $228M as mining shrank. Horizon 1 delivered for Microsoft and IREN gained NVIDIA Exemplar Cloud status.

IREN's $4B+ annualized revenue target holds but moved from end-2026 to January 2027, possibly end-February, on client network-design changes and supplier delays (Reuters: no contractual penalties); $15B of capex planned for the rest of the fiscal year. ARR is not realized GAAP revenue.

Verdict on IREN: very good commercially, mixed financially, not an aggressive buy signal in a book already concentrated in AI infrastructure; over 6-12 months he wants Microsoft capacity live, $4B+ ARR reached and new funding without excessive dilution.

themes.status: NFP 15:30 RO · CONSENSUS ~59K · S&P 7,350 / NASDAQ 24,300 WARNING LEVELS
themes.title: NFP day: three session scenarios, and the rest of the book judged on its own risks
themes.lead: He kept cash back for the jobs report, warns that a weak number is not automatically good for stocks, and runs the rest of the portfolio through one line each.
bullets: October NFP due Nov 6 at 15:30 Romania time (BLS-confirmed): consensus ~59,000 jobs after ~29,000, unemployment ~4.2%; read jobs, unemployment, wages and revisions together.
Moderate NFP supports a stabilizing-policy view; very strong with fast wage growth pushes Treasury yields up and pressures growth valuations; very weak lowers yields but feeds slowdown fears.

Session scenarios: positive (yields stable, no NFP shock, semis recover; S&P 500 back toward 7,500-7,570 is the first real test for buyers); base (volatility and consolidation, where many mistake a technical rally for fundamental confirmation); negative (losing S&P 7,350 is a further warning and Nasdaq 24,300 the immediate marker).

Rest of the GYW book: TSLA -10.77% to $343.69 (autonomy, robotics, energy, but exposed to political-risk repricing); META -3.96% to ~$605.08 (ad cash sets it apart from infrastructure builders); PLTR solid growth and profitability, but valuation amplifies volatility.

SOFI is sensitive to the economy, funding cost and credit quality, and a very weak NFP could raise credit-risk worries; HOOD gains volume from volatility but a long correction can hurt client activity.

RKLB rides contracts, Neutron and execution, and the SpaceX drop does not imply weaker prospects; ASTS depends on launches, approvals and monetizing partnerships, so size it prudently; ONDS hinges on turning orders into revenue and cash more than on short interest; LEU benefits from energy-security and nuclear-fuel interest, with contract timing and expansion financing as risks.

takeaways.title: Test each position on results, moat, growth outlook, balance sheet and fit with your risk, not on yesterday's price.
Group holdings by shared driver (AI spending, space sentiment); five names that move together are one big position.
Buy in stages at prices set in advance, and only after the price stabilizes, as he did with VRT below $192.
Keep cash back before a big data release; a weak NFP is not automatically good for stocks.
Split AI names into cash generators and capex-funded builders; financing and dilution decide the second group.
Make no permanent decision on a temporary emotion: close the charts and go back to the fundamentals.
